root_idea.summary: The root denotes twisting, plaiting, or folding something tightly, especially into a rope or cord.
root_idea.development: The concrete sense develops from twisting palm fibre and other materials into rope, with related extensions describing tightly knit, compact, or well-formed bodies.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested noun is presented under its normalized classical citation form.

senses.definition: Palm fibre, a fibrous material used to make rope.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression حَبْلٌ مِنْ مَسَدٍ, the word denotes the fibre or material of which the rope is made; the supplied Quranic context gloss is “palm-fiber.”

senses.definition: A firmly twisted rope or cord; in the Quranic expression حَبْلٌ مِنْ مَسَدٍ, a strongly twisted chain or rope.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a construction-specific Quranic interpretation of حَبْلٌ مِنْ مَسَدٍ; the classical interpretation includes a chain of firmly twisted iron, and does not make “iron” the general meaning of the noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To twist a rope, or to twist it firmly or well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verb with the infinitive مَسْدٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pursue a journey laboriously or energetically; to continue or hold to a journey.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage may refer to travel by night or to continuous travel by night or day.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make an animal lean, lank, or light of flesh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The stated causes include continued travel and leguminous herbage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the belly, to become soft, small, even, and free of ugliness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive or resultative usage describing the condition of the belly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an idiomatic expression concerning camel milk, to strengthen the upper parts of the flesh and make them firm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This meaning is attested in the cited expression rather than as a general unrestricted gloss for every occurrence of the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Well-turned, compact, and slender in build; of good stature or a well-knit frame.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person; the feminine form مَمْسُودَةٌ is also used, including for a woman who is compactly formed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a belly, soft, small, even, and without ugliness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a descriptive adjectival use distinct from the passive verbal expression مُسِدَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rope or cord, especially one plaited and firmly twisted, made from fibre, hair, wool, hide, plants, bark, or other materials.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This records the broader Classical usage beyond the Quranic palm-fibre context; the noun may refer to the rope itself as well as to its material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A back compact like a strongly twisted rope.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative descriptive expression applied to the back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An iron axis or spindle of a pulley.
A skin container for clarified butter or honey, or a black skin used for wine and similar liquids.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal form related to مِسْأَبٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Even and well-formed, goodly, or beautiful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression ساقٌ مَسْدَاءُ, describing a shank.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Twisting a rope is represented under the Form I verb.
The energetic or continuous journey sense is represented.
The causative sense of making an animal lean is represented.
The resulting condition of the belly is represented.
The specialized camel-milk expression is represented.
The feminine compact-build usage is represented with the related participial adjective.
The unit contains the fibre, rope, broader-material, and Quranic chain interpretations.
The pulley-axis technical sense is represented.
The descriptive shank expression is represented.
The unit contains both the compact-build description and the belly description.

cautions: The Quranic phrase حَبْلٌ مِنْ مَسَدٍ supports both a palm-fibre/material reading and a classical interpretation as a firmly twisted chain, including iron; these are presented as distinct constructional senses rather than as a general claim that مَسَدٌ means iron.
The Quranic occurrence is the genitive form مَسَدٍ in 111:5; the public headword is normalized to the citation form مَسَدٌ.
